en.title: Total Forward Distance After Adding Two Fuel Stations Each Time
en.description:
Vehicle positions are non-decreasing, and vehicles can only move right. Each query independently adds fuel stations at the positions of vehicles a and b, and the position of the last vehicle always has a station; each vehicle stops at the nearest station that is not to its left.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n q; the second line contains n non-decreasing position values; each of the next q lines contains a b (1-based, a<b). The original gives no value ranges; this site sets 2≤n≤100000, 1≤q≤100000, −10⁹≤position≤10⁹.
en.output: Output q total distances in query order.
en.explanation: Example 1: the five vehicles travel 3, 0, 5, 0, 0, for a total of 8. Example 2: the first two vehicles already have stations and so does the last vehicle, for a total of 0. Example 3: in both queries only one vehicle moves forward by 1, so the total distances are 1 and 1.
hints: Precompute, for each position, the rightmost index A, B sharing the same coordinate, and use prefix sums to split the vehicles into [0,A), [A,B) and [B,n), which go to the two added stations and the last station respectively; the distance of each part is count×(station position)−(sum of positions in the range).
